Things to do in Totterdown

Updated 2 November 2026. Opening hours change, so check with each place before you go. How we check facts.

Totterdown is small enough to walk around in an afternoon, but steep enough that you'll feel it. Here's what's worth seeing, starting from Temple Meads station at the bottom of the hill.

Quick answer

  • See: the coloured terraces, including Richmond Street, and Vale Street, England's steepest residential street. [1] [2]
  • Drink: the Thunderbolt, a former tollhouse, plus the Shakespeare and the Star & Dove. [3] [4] [5]
  • Eat: a fry-up at Totterdown Canteen, pizza at A Cappella, fish and chips at Farrows. [6]
  • Walk: Arnos Vale, a Victorian garden cemetery on the Bath Road, or up to Perrett's Park for one of Bristol's best skyline views. [7] [8]
  • Time it: the arts trail on 14 and 15 November 2026, or the Vale Street egg roll on Easter Sunday. [9] [10]

Where are Totterdown's coloured houses?

The painted Victorian terraces on the hillside are visible from Temple Meads and much of the city centre. [11] Richmond Street is one of the best known, with more than 70 houses, most of them brightly painted. [1] Visit Bristol's walk from Temple Meads takes you through these streets. [12]

Can you visit Vale Street?

Yes. It's a public residential street, and Ordnance Survey named it England's steepest in 2019. [2] Banksy's "Aachoo!!" mural appeared there in December 2020, but it was removed in March 2021. [13] Please respect residents' homes. Read our Vale Street guide.

What are the best pubs in Totterdown?

Totterdown pubs
PubWhy go
The Thunderbolt, 124 Bath RoadA Grade II listed former turnpike tollhouse from about 1840, known for live music [3] [14]
The Shakespeare, 1 Henry StreetA traditional local, recommended for cider [4] [6]
The OxfordRecommended for its Sunday roast [6]
Star & Dove, St Luke's RoadA pub and dining room in the heart of Totterdown, also showing sport [5] [6]

Bruhaha, a nano brewery and bar, is another local suggestion for an evening out. [6]

Where to eat in Totterdown

Most of Totterdown's cafés and restaurants are on and around the Wells Road. Visit Bristol's locals' guide recommends: [6]

  • Totterdown Canteen: a cooked breakfast.
  • Farrows: fish and chips.
  • A Cappella: pizza.

Places open and close, so check opening times before you set off.

Where are the best views of Bristol from Totterdown?

  • Perrett's Park: on the edge of Totterdown, Windmill Hill and Knowle, it's one of the city's best-known viewpoints, and a popular spot to watch the Bristol International Balloon Fiesta's mass ascents in August. [8]
  • Victoria Park: next door in Windmill Hill, with views over Totterdown and central Bristol. [15]
  • From the streets: the top of almost any Totterdown street looks out across the city, and Temple Meads looks back at the coloured houses. [11]

Is Arnos Vale Cemetery worth visiting?

Arnos Vale is a Victorian garden cemetery on the Bath Road, on the edge of Totterdown. Its first burial was in 1839. [7] [16]

  • Design: it was laid out in the style of a Greek necropolis, influenced by Père Lachaise in Paris. [16]
  • Rescued: after decades of decline, Bristol City Council took ownership in 2003 and a charitable trust was set up to restore it. [7]
  • Still working: it's still an active cemetery, so be respectful of services. [7]

What landmarks can you see on the way?

  • Three Lamps: the Grade II* listed signpost pointing to Bath and Wells, at the top of Bath Road. [17]
  • Bristol Jamia Mosque: on Green Street, the first mosque in Bristol, in a former church. [18]
  • Totterdown Bridge: the 1888 bridge over the Avon at the foot of the hill. [19]

The stories behind them are in our history of Totterdown.
